rationale.conceptual: Standard ab initio melt-quench protocol for amorphous materials using plane-wave DFT; involves understanding of molecular dynamics, thermostats, finite-displacement phonons, and density-of-states projection, but no novel algorithms.
rationale.execution: Multi-step pipeline: setting up and running AIMD with Quantum ESPRESSO, calculating the dynamical matrix via finite differences, and post-processing for RDF and EDOS; requires careful handling of DFT input parameters and dependencies between stages.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper presents a standard ab initio melt-quench simulation of amorphous carbon using plane-wave DFT. Reproducing the 120-atom model and derived properties (RDF, VDOS, EDOS) requires careful implementation of well-known methods (MD, phonon calculations, DOS projection) but no novel algorithms. The pipeline is moderately complex with four interdependent stages and external DFT tooling.

compute_estimate.reasoning: 120‑atom system, 15 ps melt‑quench MD with DFT is the main cost; moderate CPU cluster and ~16 GB RAM sufficient; data volume negligible.
